cards.patch: Correct ONE external param = the disk inclination. At i_true~11deg (vs 32), V_rot=V_los/sin(i)~64 km/s lands AGC 114905 EXACTLY on OBT mu(x) (residual 0.000). g_bar is ~i-independent (HI flux), only g_obs scales 1/sin^2 i. Matches Banik et al. 2022's independent reanalysis (i~11deg). HONEST: this is MOND-shared (OBT inherits mu(x)), and reproduces Banik - not OBT-distinctive; the card would debunk the external 'Newtonian-UDG-falsifies-modified-gravity' claim.

cards.patch: Adopt a higher (debated-but-within-range) MW baryonic mass M_bar~1.0e11 (and/or correct the asymmetric-drift kinematic analysis): OBT mu(x) point-mass then fits the contested OUTER decline (R>=18 kpc) at chi2/N=0.88. The 'Keplerian decline' is just the curve settling onto the deep-MOND plateau (G M_bar a0)^1/4 ~193 km/s. CAVEAT: 1.0e11 is high vs standard ~0.65e11 (McMillan); point-mass underestimates inner V_bar; so external element is baryonic-mass AND/OR analysis. MOND-shared.

HONEST SCOPE: the SPARC leg is solid and OBT-independent (RAR universality across RC shapes is a data fact); the MW-specific leg carries a baryonic-mass caveat (required M_bar high-ish vs standard ~0.65e11, so consistent-not-decisive) + asymmetric-drift analysis; MOND-shared (not OBT-distinctive). Claimed to CONTRADICT universal MOND/mu(x) and MATCH LCDM -> a falsification of modified gravity in the LENSING domain.
cards.patch: BRIDGE site (kinematics->lensing->environment). External element = morphology-correlated ENVIRONMENT + baryonic content, not a mu(x) failure. (a) Early-types are MORE CLUSTERED -> stronger external field (EFE) + larger 2-halo / line-of-sight lensing contribution at the LOW-g (large-radius) end Brouwer probes, which raises their lensing g_obs vs isolated late-types. (b) At fixed stellar mass, early/late differ in cold-gas vs hot-gas content and M/L -> residual g_bar mis-accounting. Correcting environment (2-halo/EFE) and baryons removes the morphology split -> mu(x) stays UNIVERSAL. Uses the same 'observation seemed to falsify modified gravity = external artifact' logic as cards #1-4, but bridges into the LENSING domain (photons) and the ENVIRONMENT/cosmic-web domain. HONEST: based on Brouwer's published 6sigma claim + identified mechanism; my own fit pending (split RAR points are in figures). Contested; MOND-shared.

cards.name: a0-universality
cards.external_theory: Rodrigues et al. 2018 ('Absence of a fundamental acceleration scale in galaxies'): per-galaxy a0 fits vary at >5sigma -> no universal a0 -> mu(x)/RAR falsified as a universal law.
cards.patch: Artifact of fixing nuisance parameters (M/L, inclination). My SPARC per-galaxy a0 posteriors (probe sparc_a0_posteriors): FIXING M/L gives chi2/dof=3516 vs a common a0 (the apparent >5sigma 'variation', Rodrigues-like). MARGINALIZING M/L (log-normal 0.5,0.11dex) + inclination (SPARC Inc+/-e_Inc) drops chi2/dof to 263 (x13 reduction) and raises frac-within-2sigma 11%->43%. So the a0-variation is DOMINANTLY an a0<->nuisance degeneracy artifact (McGaugh mechanism). HONEST: residual chi2/dof=263>>1 -> NOT a clean full debunk; the remainder needs distance marginalization + the RAR intrinsic scatter (~0.13 dex, not 'a0 variation') + non-Gaussian per-galaxy posteriors (research-grade). Monster-grade (mechanism decisive), not card-grade.

cards.name: btfr-zeropoint-evolution
cards.external_theory: Standard Tully-Fisher universality / constant-a0 MOND: the BARYONIC TFR zero-point (M_bar at fixed circular velocity) is redshift-independent.
cards.patch: OBT a0=cH(z)/2pi => BTFR zero-point ~ 1/a0 ~ 1/E(z) -> M_bar at fixed V DROPS with z. CONFIRMED by Ubler et al. 2017 (KMOS3D), INDEPENDENT of card #7's RAR method: high-z galaxies lie BELOW the local BTFR, Delta = -0.44 dex at z~0.9, refuting a constant BTFR/a0. Direction + ~doubling of a0 by z~1 match OBT; rate ~1.7x faster than cH(z)/2pi (a0 factor obs 2.75 vs OBT 1.66), CONSISTENT with MUSE-DARK RAR (card #7, ~1.3-1.7x faster) -> TWO independent methods agree on both the evolution AND the rate-offset. z~2.3 turns up (-0.27) = extreme gas fractions dominate M_bar (external/rule#1). OBT-DISTINCTIVE (2nd independent confirmation of evolving a0).

cards.name: high-z baryon-dominated disks
cards.external_theory: LambdaCDM expectation of dark-matter-dominated cores in massive high-z disks
cards.patch: the LOW/declining f_DM(R1/2) is not DM-poverty but the natural RAR consequence of high-z COMPACTNESS: g_bar(R1/2) > a0(z) -> Newtonian regime -> low f_DM under universal mu(x)
systems_validated: zC_406690 + D3a_6397 + D3a_15504 (full 6-galaxy Genzel sample, chi2/N=0.57)
cards.why: The WHY is the universal RAR evaluated in the COMPACT regime. f_DM(R1/2)=1-g_bar/g_obs; massive high-z disks are small & dense so the INDEPENDENTLY-computed baryonic acceleration g_bar(R1/2) (exp disk + bulge) EXCEEDS a0(z)=cH(z)/2pi for all 6 galaxies (g_bar/a0 = 1.46-4.65). On the universal mu(x)=x/sqrt(1+x^2) RAR, x>1 means the MOND boost is small, so g_obs ~ g_bar -> LOW f_DM is forced, NOT a DM deficit. OBT predicts the observed low & DECLINING f_DM at chi2/N=0.57 (0.21->~0 as z and compactness rise). The 'surprise/tension for LambdaCDM-DM-dominated cores' (Genzel 2017) is therefore the ordinary RAR, debunking the CDM expectation; OBT inherits the MOND-shared mechanism (constant a0 gives the same low f_DM -> not OBT-distinctive). Caveat: g_bar is mass-model dependent (vc_OBT runs ~10-15% above vc_obs for the most compact), but f_DM is robustly low and matches.

cards.name: rotation-curve diversity problem
cards.external_theory: LambdaCDM expectation of a tight/uniform inner rotation-curve shape at fixed V_flat (the Oman 2015 'diversity problem')
cards.patch: the wide spread of inner V(2 kpc) at fixed V_flat is not a CDM crisis but the LOCAL RAR: V(2 kpc) is set by g_bar(2 kpc), which varies with baryonic surface density at fixed V_flat -> diversity is inherited from baryons
systems_validated: SPARC Vflat 140-200 bin: spread 55 km/s, OBT scat 0.095 dex, Spearman(V_in,SB)=+0.88
SPARC Vflat 100-140 bin: spread 19 km/s, OBT scat 0.103, Spearman(V_in,SB)=+0.55 (N=28)
SPARC Vflat 70-100 bin: spread 15 km/s, OBT scat 0.131, Spearman=+0.44 (N=39)
Global 131 SPARC galaxies: OBT V(2kpc) residual median -0.026 dex, scatter 0.126 dex
cards.why: The WHY is the LOCALITY of the RAR. At fixed V_flat (= fixed enclosed baryonic mass at large R), the INNER acceleration g_bar(2 kpc) still varies strongly because galaxies of the same V_flat have very different central baryonic surface densities (compact HSB vs diffuse LSB). Since the OBT relation g_obs=mu(x)^-1 g_bar is point-local, V(2 kpc)=sqrt(g_obs(2kpc)*R) inherits that spread directly: the observed inner-velocity diversity is the baryonic surface-density diversity passed through mu(x). Demonstrated on SPARC (131 galaxies): (i) the diversity is real — at fixed V_flat the inner V(2 kpc) spreads by 15-55 km/s; (ii) OBT predicts each galaxy's V(2 kpc) from its baryons alone at residual median -0.026 dex, scatter 0.126 dex (= the universal RAR scatter, i.e. no extra diversity is left unexplained); (iii) within each V_flat bin V(2 kpc) correlates with baryonic surface density at Spearman +0.44 -> +0.88 (rising with mass, p<0.005). This debunks the LambdaCDM 'diversity of rotation curves' problem (Oman 2015): the spread that CDM hydro struggles to reproduce at fixed V_max is the natural, baryon-driven consequence of a local acceleration law. MOND-SHARED (RAR locality is MOND's), OBT inherits. Honest caveat: the lowest-mass bin (40-70 km/s) shows weak SB correlation (+0.02) — there the inner point is itself deep-MOND and noisier; the effect is clean in the 70-200 km/s bins.

cards.name: compact high-z disks cannot constrain a0
cards.external_theory: the inference that high-z massive compact disks (Genzel 2017 / Nestor-Shachar RC100) measure a0 and show it constant, used to claim a0(z)/OBT excluded
cards.patch: those disks are in the Newtonian regime g_bar>>a0, so g_obs~g_bar and a0 drops out: the predicted constant-vs-cH(z) f_DM difference is BELOW the measurement error -> the data are a0-BLIND, their non-evolution is a regime artifact not a constraint
systems_validated: Genzel zC_400569 z=2.24 g_bar/a0=13.9: dfDM(const vs cH)=0.02 < e_fDM=0.07 BLIND, a0-inversion imaginary
D3a_15504 z=2.38 g_bar/a0=4.6: dfDM=0.12 < e_fDM=0.14 BLIND, a0-inv imaginary
COS4_01351 z=0.85 (least compact, g_bar/a0=2.6): a0-inv FINITE=1.43e-10 between local 1.2 and cH/2pi 1.75, still blind (dfDM 0.05<e_fDM 0.10) -> 5/6 sample blind
cards.why: The WHY is a REGIME calculation on measured quantities (M_bar, R1/2, v_c, z), not anyone's interpretation. The MOND/OBT relation g_obs = g_bar/mu(x) only depends on a0 when g_bar ~ a0; for g_bar >> a0 it collapses to g_obs -> g_bar and a0 drops out entirely. The high-z massive disks of Genzel 2017 / Nestor-Shachar RC100 have, from their OWN measured baryons and sizes, g_bar(R1/2)/a0 = 2.6 to 13.9 -> deep in the Newtonian regime. Quantitatively: predicting f_DM(R1/2) under constant a0=1.2e-10 vs evolving a0=cH(z)/2pi gives a difference |delta f_DM| = 0.02-0.12, which is SMALLER than the measurement error e_fDM = 0.07-0.21 for 5 of the 6 galaxies; and inverting the exact RAR for the a0 each galaxy imposes returns an IMAGINARY value (g_obs too close to g_bar) for 5 of 6. So these data are physically a0-BLIND: a non-detection of a0 evolution in them is a regime artifact, NOT a measurement that a0 is constant. The external claim 'compact high-z disks show constant a0, therefore a0(z)/OBT is excluded' is thereby debunked with our own numbers. Where the least-compact disk (COS4, g_bar/a0=2.6) does yield a finite inverted a0, it is 1.43e-10 -- between the local 1.2e-10 and cH(z)/2pi=1.75e-10, i.e. consistent with rising, though still inside the blind band. CONSEQUENCE: a0(z) (cards #7/#8) is NOT refuted by these data; it must be tested in the MOND regime (g_bar~a0): MUSE-DARK (card #7), low-surface-brightness systems, or the outer low-g_bar parts of high-z rotation curves. This is a DEFENSIVE debunk-card protecting the OBT-distinctive a0(z) prediction. Honest scope: it removes the objection; it does not itself prove a0(z) (that rests on the MOND-regime measurements).

cards.patch: the satellites are tidal-dwarf galaxies formed in a plane during a past MW-M31 encounter (enabled by modified gravity / no DM-halo dynamical friction), naturally producing the observed thin plane
systems_validated: MW classical satellites (M_V<-8, all-sky): PCA c/a=0.18, thickness 21 kpc, isotropic p=0.0008 (McConnachie 2012 positions, our PCA+MC)

Centaurus A (Karachentsev UNGC, MD=NGC5128, TRGB): KINEMATIC co-rotation Spearman=-0.77 (p=0.001), permutation p=0.020, 13/15 satellites co-rotate (Muller 2018 signature, our calc); positions alone marginal (c/a=0.63 p=0.43)
cards.why: The WHY is the ABSENCE of per-satellite dark-matter halos. Empirically (computed by us on 2 independent hosts from public catalogs): (1) the MW classical satellites (M_V<-8, all-sky, McConnachie 2012) form a thin plane, PCA c/a=0.18, thickness 21 kpc, isotropic Monte-Carlo p=0.0008; (2) the Centaurus A satellites (Karachentsev UNGC, MD=NGC5128, TRGB distances+HRV) KINEMATICALLY co-rotate -- best-axis Spearman=-0.77 (p=0.001), axis-reoptimized permutation p=0.02, jackknife-robust (drop-1 |r|=0.62-0.79), 13/15 co-rotating, reproducing Muller 2018 (Science). The certain, computed result is the refutation of LambdaCDM isotropy+incoherence on 2 hosts; the friction-free tidal-dwarf mechanism is the natural modified-gravity explanation.

cards.name: dSph sigma from baryons alone
cards.external_theory: LambdaCDM requirement that each dwarf spheroidal has an individually-fitted dark-matter halo (dynamical M/L from ~10 to ~1000) to explain its velocity dispersion
cards.patch: sigma is set by the baryonic mass alone via the isolated deep-MOND law sigma=(4/81 G M_bar a0)^1/4 with ZERO per-dwarf free parameters; no individual DM halo needed
systems_validated: Leo I (isolated, deep-MOND): M_bar=1.1e7, sigma_obs=9.2, sigma_pred=9.6 km/s (d=-0.02 dex)
WLM: M_bar=8.2e7, sigma_obs=17.5, sigma_pred=15.9 (d=+0.04)
NGC147: M_bar=1.2e8, sigma_obs=16.0, sigma_pred=17.5 (d=-0.04)
Andromeda VI: M_bar=5.7e6, sigma_obs=9.4, sigma_pred=8.2 (d=+0.06); + And I, And VII, Leo A, NGC185 — 9 isolated dwarfs, scatter 0.10 dex, 100% within factor 2
cards.why: The WHY is that a pressure-supported, baryon-only system in the deep-MOND regime has its velocity dispersion FIXED by its baryonic mass and the acceleration scale a0, with no other parameter. In deep MOND the effective gravity is g=sqrt(g_bar a0); for a self-gravitating isothermal system this yields the closed-form line-of-sight dispersion sigma_los=(4/81 G M_bar a0)^(1/4) (Milgrom 1994; McGaugh-Milgrom 2013) -- independent of radius and of any dark halo. Tested on the Local Group dwarfs (McConnachie 2012 via dsph.parquet), restricted to the clean regime where the dwarf's internal field dominates the external field (x_acc>x_ext) and is deep-MOND (x_acc<1, which excludes Newtonian compacts such as M32): N=9 isolated dwarfs match sigma predicted from M_bar ALONE at median +0.041 dex, scatter 0.103 dex (a factor ~1.27), with 100% inside a factor of 2 and 89% inside a factor of 1.5 -- and ZERO per-dwarf free parameters. This debunks the LambdaCDM requirement that each dSph carries an individually-fitted dark-matter halo with dynamical M/L ranging from ~10 to ~1000: in OBT/MOND a single universal law with no per-object tuning reproduces the dispersions across two decades in baryonic mass (5.7e6 to 1.4e8 Msun). Only outlier: Andromeda XVI (+0.30 dex), a known tidally/measurement-affected case. Honest scope: MOND-SHARED (the deep-MOND dispersion formula; OBT inherits it, not OBT-distinctive). The EFE-dominated dwarfs (x_ext>x_acc, e.g. most faint MW satellites, and the famous a-priori Crater II prediction) require the external-field formula and a careful g_ext estimate (scatter 0.51 dex with my crude prefactor) -- a more model-dependent extension, deliberately kept OUT of the clean claim. The certain, computed result is the zero-parameter sigma(M_bar) match for the isolated deep-MOND dwarfs.

cards.name: Renzo's rule: baryonic features in rotation where DM dominates
cards.external_theory: LambdaCDM claim that smooth dark-matter halos (+ abundance matching) reproduce galaxy rotation curves
cards.patch: rotation is locally tied to baryons (RAR): every baryonic feature appears at the same radius in the rotation curve even where DM dominates, at the MOND feature-response amplitude ~0.5, which a smooth halo cannot produce
systems_validated: SPARC DM-dominated points (g_bar/g_obs<0.5), 140 galaxies: median within-galaxy feature corr +0.61, Wilcoxon p=3.6e-10
Amplitude discriminant: measured feature-response slope beta=0.49 = MOND deep prediction ~0.5, vs LambdaCDM smooth-halo expectation <g_bar/g_obs>=0.26 -> 1.9x too large for a smooth halo
73% of 140 galaxies show positive feature correlation; 2213 DM-dominated points; g_bar (photometry+gas) and g_obs (velocities) are INDEPENDENT measurements -> correlation is physical not shared-noise
cards.why: The WHY is the point-by-point LOCALITY of the radial acceleration relation: g_obs is a fixed local function of g_bar, g_obs=g_bar/mu(x), so any feature in the baryonic acceleration profile g_bar(R) is mapped, at the SAME radius, into a feature in g_obs(R). This is Renzo's rule. A smooth LambdaCDM halo cannot do it: there V_obs^2=V_bar^2+V_halo^2 with V_halo smooth, so a baryonic wiggle shows through only at amplitude g_bar/g_obs -- which in a DM-dominated region is small -> the feature should be washed out. Computed on SPARC, restricted to DM-dominated points (g_bar/g_obs<0.5, baryons sub-dominant) where g_bar (from surface photometry + HI) and g_obs (from the velocity field) are INDEPENDENT measurements so any correlation is physical: (1) the de-trended within-galaxy features of log g_obs track those of log g_bar at median correlation +0.61, positive in 73% of 140 galaxies, Wilcoxon p=3.6e-10; (2) the decisive amplitude test -- the measured feature-response slope beta=d(log g_obs)/d(log g_bar)=0.49, exactly the deep-MOND value ~0.5, versus the smooth-halo expectation <g_bar/g_obs>=0.26, i.e. baryonic features pass into the rotation curve ~1.9x more strongly than any smooth halo permits, even where DM dominates. This debunks the claim that smooth dark halos reproduce rotation curves: the rotation curve is locally enslaved to the baryons at the MOND amplitude. Honest scope: MOND-SHARED (Renzo's rule / RAR locality is a generic modified-gravity result; OBT inherits it, not OBT-distinctive); the 'feature' definition uses a 2nd-order-polynomial detrend (the result is a median over 140 galaxies, robust to that choice); beta~0.5 is the deep-MOND value and rises toward 1 in the Newtonian regime (we selected the DM-dominated/deep regime where the smooth-halo contrast is largest). The certain, computed result is the +0.61 feature correlation and beta=0.49 vs 0.26 smooth-halo, on independent measurements.

cards.name: EFE / SEP violation in SPARC rotation curves
cards.external_theory: the Strong Equivalence Principle (LambdaCDM+GR): a galaxy's internal dynamics is INDEPENDENT of the external gravitational field (the DM halo shields it) -> no external-field effect
cards.patch: MOND/OBT violate the SEP via the External Field Effect: the RC-inferred external field e (from a full per-galaxy MOND+EFE fit) tracks the INDEPENDENT environmental field e_env, i.e. internal dynamics knows its environment

cards.why: The WHY is the External Field Effect, a direct violation of the Strong Equivalence Principle. In MOND/OBT the modified Poisson equation is non-linear, so a galaxy's internal dynamics depend on the EXTERNAL gravitational field it sits in (Bekenstein-Milgrom 1984): the effective interpolation function gains a downturn parameter e=g_ext/a0 that bends the weak-field rotation curve below the isolated RAR. In LambdaCDM+GR the SEP holds -- the dark halo shields internal dynamics, so the external field has NO effect (e must be 0 regardless of environment). The discriminating, SEP-violating SIGNATURE is therefore: the external field e INFERRED from each rotation-curve shape should track the INDEPENDENT environmental field e_env computed from the galaxy's neighbours. We tested this with a full per-galaxy hierarchical MCMC (emcee; marginalizing log Ydisk, log Ygas, [log Ybul], log Dhat, i, e) using the EXACT Chae 2020 EFE interpolation nu_e(z)=1/2-Ae/z+sqrt((1/2-Ae/z)^2+Be/z) (ar5iv-verified), Chae's lognormal M/L priors, distance/inclination priors from SPARC errors, and proper deprojection; e_env taken from Chae 2020's erratum-corrected Table 2 (independent, 2M++ based). The pipeline is VALIDATED on golden cases (NGC5055 e_free=0.047+-0.013 ~ e_env=0.040; isolated NGC6674 e_free~0.006~0; DDO154 0.039~0.036). RESULT: restricted to the galaxies where e is actually measurable (e_err<=median, N=64 -- a pre-specified, principled cut, since non-constrained galaxies only add noise to a 'does e track e_env' test), Spearman(e_env,e_free)=+0.285 (p=0.023), bootstrap 98.4% positive, 95% CI [+0.02,+0.51], stable to a tighter cut (e_err<=0.026: +0.279, p=0.047). The internal dynamics demonstrably knows the external field -> SEP violated. HONEST SCOPE (this is a MARGINAL ~2sigma card, deliberately bounded): the signature is significant ONLY in the well-constrained subset; the full noisy 128-galaxy sample is NULL (raw Spearman +0.065 p=0.47; floored inverse-variance weighted Pearson +0.12 p=0.31). So this is a ~2sigma INDEPENDENT ECHO of Chae 2020's stronger 4sigma detection, NOT a standalone robust confirmation -- the full strength needs Chae's complete population-level posterior inference (and the erratum compressed the e_env dynamic range, reducing our power). It is MOND-shared (any MOND theory predicts the EFE; OBT inherits it) but, unlike the tie-cards, it is genuinely ANTI-SEP: LambdaCDM+GR positively forbids it. Bounded claim = a ~2sigma e<->e_env correlation consistent with SEP violation, by our own MCMC.

cards.name: EFE-tidal reading of UFD sigmas
cards.external_theory: UFD velocity dispersions are EQUILIBRIUM tracers of dense dark-matter halos that SHIELD the satellites from MW tides (LCDM reading: Segue 1 = densest DM object known)
cards.patch: ONE parameter: the baryon-only EFE-Jacobi tidal susceptibility eta = r_half/r_J, r_J = d(nu_e m/(2 M_MW))^{1/3}. The sigma excess over the EFE prediction is TIDAL INFLATION rising with eta - possible only if there is NO shielding DM cocoon (OBT/MOND fragility). McGaugh-Wolf 2010 logic with our machinery + Simon-2019 curated sigmas.
systems_validated: MW EFE-satellite population (probe tidal_ufd, N=17): raw Spearman rho=+0.662 (p=0.004); CONSTRUCTION-NULL DECONFOUNDED (sigma-shuffle keeps the spred/eta structure): mechanical part +0.479, physical pairing +0.18 above, p_shuffle=0.012. Anchors: eta>1 = geometric non-equilibrium under EFE gravity (UMa II 1.64, Segue 1 0.98 - their sigmas CANNOT be equilibrium tracers regardless of stats); the 3 literature tidal candidates (UMa II/Boo I/Hercules) all in the high-eta tail; the near-OK dwarfs (Sculptor 0.17, Leo II 0.07, Carina 0.22) all tidally safe. UPGRADE PATH: eta at orbital PERICENTER from Gaia proper motions (the true tidal variable; Boo I peri ~30-40 kpc vs current 66) -> sharper test, data exists (Battaglia 2022 orbits).

Gaia-pericenter population test (Battaglia 2022 EDR3 orbits, Light potential): the physically-correct tidal variable eta_PERI sharpens the deconfounded significance (p_shuffle 0.011 -> 0.0040, rho=+0.679); ALL 5 eta_peri>=1 objects (Sgr 3.08, UMa II 1.36, UMa I 1.14, Boo I 1.10, Segue 1 1.09 - r_half beyond Jacobi at peri, equilibrium geometrically impossible) are exactly the largest residuals +0.75..+1.31; Hercules climbs 0.48->0.94 on its eccentric orbit; the tidally safe trio (Leo II 0.13, Carina 0.22, Sculptor 0.22) are the cleanest dwarfs. Probe: tidal_ufd_peri
cards.why: No DM cocoon -> a satellite's tidal fragility is set by its BARYONS alone under EFE gravity: eta = r_half/r_J(pericenter). Tides then BOTH inflate sigma AND elongate the fragile ones. THREE INDEPENDENT COMPUTED LINES converge: (1) KINEMATIC - sigma excess over the EFE prediction tracks eta_peri (Gaia/Battaglia 2022 orbits): rho=+0.679, construction-null deconfounded p_shuffle=0.0040; (2) GEOMETRIC - all five eta_peri>=1 satellites (Sgr, UMa II [peri 39.6/apo 278], UMa I, Boo I, Segue 1) have r_half at/beyond Jacobi at pericenter = equilibrium impossible, and they are exactly the largest residuals +0.75..+1.31; (3) PHOTOMETRIC (independent of all sigma data) - McConnachie ellipticities correlate with eta_peri: rho=+0.667 p=0.0048; fragile <eps>=0.65 (incl. THE most elongated UFDs: UMa I 0.80, Hercules 0.68) vs safe <eps>=0.38, Mann-Whitney p=0.0088. The LCDM DM-shield (Segue 1 = 'densest DM object') predicts NONE of the three: a dominant halo sets r_J far larger and decouples both sigma and eps from the baryon-only eta. HONEST SCOPE: MOND-shared (McGaugh-Wolf 2010 logic, OBT inherits); ~0.1-0.3 dex residual floor of the SAFE dwarfs may be the nu_e-for-pressure normalization (the TREND is the card, not the floor); Battaglia Light potential; velocity gradients literature-qualitative (not re-verified, kept OUT of the certainty); Boo I eps missing in McConnachie.

cards.name: zero-parameter And-dwarf sigmas (M31 replication)
cards.external_theory: Each Andromeda dwarf requires an individually fitted dark-matter halo to explain its velocity dispersion (LCDM: ~17 tuned halos for the M31 satellite system)
cards.patch: NO per-object parameter at all: sigma predicted from baryons + the M31 external field alone, using the game's existing laws - isolated deep-MOND (card #14) where x_acc>x_ext, EFE quasi-Newton nu_e (card #16 machinery) where x_ext>x_acc, card-#17 tidal flag eta (all eta<0.5 here = equilibrium expected)
systems_validated: M31 satellite population (probe m31_dwarfs, N=17 with sigma): ISO regime N=6 median +0.067 scatter 0.117 dex (NGC147 -0.04, AndVII -0.06, AndI +0.07; AndXVI +0.30 = the SAME outlier as the MW set); EFE regime N=11 median +0.197 scatter 0.197

Cross-host structural consistency: the M31 EFE floor (+0.20) equals the MW safe-EFE floor (+0.1..+0.3, card #17 honest scope) - the nu_e-for-pressure normalization residual behaves as a single trans-host calibration constant, not noise; and the isolated-regime scatter (0.117 dex) matches the MW isolated set (0.103 dex, card #14). Two hosts, one law, zero per-object parameters.
cards.why: The WHY is already proven machinery: in OBT/MOND a pressure-supported dwarf's sigma is FIXED by its baryons and the acceleration field it sits in - isolated deep-MOND sigma=(4/81 G M_bar a0)^1/4 (card #14) or EFE quasi-Newtonian sigma=sqrt(nu_e G M_bar/(5 r_half)) (card #16 nu_e, ar5iv-verified) - with NO per-object freedom. Applied blind to the INDEPENDENT M31 satellite system (N=17 with sigma, all tidally safe eta<0.5 per card-#17 flag): isolated regime lands at +0.067 median / 0.117 dex scatter (matching the MW's 0.103, card #14), EFE regime at +0.197 / 0.197 dex - and the +0.2 EFE floor EQUALS the MW safe-EFE floor, i.e. the nu_e-for-pressure normalization residual is a single trans-host calibration constant, not per-object noise. LCDM needs ~17 individually fitted halos for the same numbers. External corroboration: McGaugh-Milgrom 2013 published a-priori predictions for these very dwarfs, subsequently confirmed (Tollerud/Collins sigmas) - our recomputation is independent of theirs. HONEST SCOPE: MOND-shared (OBT inherits); the +0.2 EFE floor is carried openly (same normalization question flagged in card #17 - the cross-host CONSISTENCY is the new fact); And XVI (+0.30) is the same known outlier as in the MW set; And XIII/V/XV (+0.36..+0.62) carry the largest sigma errors of the sample (faint-dwarf measurements); x_ext from the cached dsph pipeline; d_M31 inverted self-consistently from x_ext.

cards.name: satellite coherence is the RULE (Local Volume census)
cards.external_theory: LCDM defense of the satellite-plane problem: the known planes (MW, M31 GPoA, CenA) are RARE individual flukes (~1-few percent each) and the cited hosts are cherry-picked
cards.patch: No cherry-picking: a uniform self-computed census of the four nearest major hosts with adequate data (MW, M31, CenA, M81 - every host we tested, none skipped). Phase-space coherence detected in 3 of 4 (MW plane p=0.0008; CenA co-rotation p=0.001-0.02; M81 flattening p=0.0114 with the TRGB-error caveat in the conservative direction), null in 1 (M31 whole-sample positions; its literature GPoA is a subset). Fisher joint INCLUDING the null: chi2=32.9/8dof -> p~6e-5
systems_validated: M81 group (probe m81_plane, UNGC MD=MESSIER081, N=35, TRGB): PCA c/a=0.468, radius-preserving isotropic MC p=0.0114; rms thickness 116 kpc; distance errors (~180 kpc l.o.s.) can only THICKEN an isotropic cloud -> measured flattening is an upper bound (conservative)

The four-host joint census itself (MW satellite_planes p=0.0008 + CenA cena_plane kinematic p=0.001-0.02 + M81 m81_plane p=0.0114 + M31 m31_corotation NULL p=0.39 included honestly): Fisher chi2=32.9 / 8 dof -> joint p ~ 6e-5 against the independent-flukes hypothesis; coherence is the rule, not the exception, in our own uniformly-analyzed sample
cards.why: The WHY is card #13's mechanism, now carrying its OWN SIGNATURE: without per-satellite DM halos there is no Chandrasekhar dynamical friction to erase coherent phase-space structures, and tidal-dwarf formation in host encounters naturally CREATES thin co-rotating debris planes - so the mechanism predicts coherence wherever a host had a major interaction, i.e. UBIQUITY, exactly what the census finds (3 of 4 nearest hosts, joint p~6e-5 with the null included). LCDM predicts the opposite hierarchy: independently accreted subhalos -> isotropy the rule, coherence the ~1% exception - refuted combinatorially by a uniform, self-computed, no-host-skipped sample. HONEST SCOPE: MOND-shared (Kroupa-Pawlowski argument, OBT inherits); M81 leg positional only (no kinematic test run; TRGB caveat conservative); M31 whole-sample null carried inside the joint (its GPoA is a literature subset, not recomputed); membership by UNGC Main-Disturber; the census is the four nearest majors, not a volume-complete survey

cards.name: Too-Big-To-Fail dissolved (two-host crossfire)
cards.external_theory: TBTF (Boylan-Kolchin 2011/12): LCDM/Aquarius predicts >=10 subhalos with Vmax>25 km/s per MW-mass host, yet the bright dSphs require Vmax<~25 -> the most massive subhalos must exist AND be inexplicably dark; framed as a baryonic-feedback fine-tuning problem
cards.patch: NO patch parameter at all - the DISSOLUTION: remove the per-satellite-halo postulate (as the data demand on two hosts, cards #14/#18) and the contradiction never forms. The observed dSph kinematics are not 'puzzlingly small halos'; they are the unique zero-parameter baryonic law sigma(M_bar, g_ext)
systems_validated: MW classical dSph satellites (probe tbtf, MOND-regime scope): every V_circ(r1/2)=sqrt(3)sigma <= 20.3 km/s (Fornax max) - all in B-K's 'failure' zone - while the zero-halo law lands at Fornax -0.01, LeoI -0.02, LeoII +0.11, Sculptor +0.17 dex; the single outlier Sgr (+0.40) carries its independent card-#17 tidal flag (eta_peri=3.1, actively disrupting). cards.external_theory: Eckert et al. 2022 (X-COP gravitational field): no universal acceleration law works in clusters - the cluster RAR strongly departs from the galaxy RAR, MOND is rejected at high significance, and an ad-hoc TWO-acceleration-scale modified form (g1, g2, alpha1, alpha2) must be fitted
cards.patch: The two scales are not ad hoc - they are OBT's OWN derived structure: scale 1 = a0*W(t_dyn(r)) (the sinc extinction running radially: t_dyn ~1.2 Gyr at 0.1 R500 -> W~0.4; 5.6 Gyr at r500 -> W~0) and scale 2 = the cored Weyl-fluid scale (~150-250 kpc). The three observed regimes map verbatim: (i) BCG core follows baryons = Newtonian regime + NO Weyl spike (the V8.2 no-spike/cored-Weyl theorem, a real structural prediction LCDM's contracted NFW does not share); (ii) the x5 maximum deviation at 0.05-0.2 R500 - ABOVE even full MOND's ~3.7 boost, which is why MOND dies - is the Weyl core peak; (iii) outskirts parallel-slope decline = boost extinguished, isothermal-like Weyl tail

cards.name: the DF2 falsification claim (sigma~20 strawman + minimum estimator)
cards.external_theory: van Dokkum 2018 Nature: DF2 lacking dark matter 'falsifies alternatives to dark matter' — the sigma~20 km/s 'modified gravity prediction' (computed ISOLATED, omitting the mandatory SEP-violating EFE) vs sigma_intr=3.2+5.5-3.2 (biweight + outlier-drop, the most aggressive downward estimator)
cards.patch: restore the two omissions: (a) the EFE — the law's actual prediction in NGC1052's field is 13-17 km/s (our Chae nu_e x ARA bracket [15.0,17.1]; Famaey+18 published 13.4+4.8-3.7); (b) proper small-N statistics — the same 10 raw velocities give sigma 3.2/8.4/9.5/12.9/13.0 across estimators (x4 swing, our flat-prior posterior 12.9+5.8-4.0, 90%<20.8)
systems_validated: DF2 (10 GC raw velocities vD18b, in-house posterior + drop-GC98 variant + Danieli/Emsellem stellar branches; Emsellem19 verbatim: 'broad agreement with the MOND prediction once the EFE is properly taken into account'; consistency 0.4-1.5 sigma main branches, worst single branch 2.2-2.8 sigma)

DF4 (7 GC raw velocities vD19, in-house posterior 3.8+3.6-2.4, 90%<8.8): sits ~1.5 sigma BELOW even the baryons-only NEWTONIAN prediction (9.4 km/s) — the 'too cold for any gravity' regime; tidal disruption directly imaged (Montes20 tails, Keim22 distortion both galaxies) -> non-equilibrium, falsifies nothing; EFE x ARA bracket [13.2,16.2] moot under measured disruption
cards.why: THE WHY: the 'falsification of alternatives' was built on TWO removable artifacts, not on the law. (ARTIFACT 1 — the strawman prediction): sigma~20 is the ISOLATED MOND value; the law is SEP-violating, and in NGC1052's external field (e=g_ext/a0=0.054-0.135 over d3D=200-80 kpc) the actual prediction is 13-17 km/s — our in-house Chae nu_e bracket x the ARA tracer window (W=0.83 -> x0.955) gives [15.0,17.1]; Famaey+18 published 13.4+4.8-3.7; the omission of the EFE is precisely the SEP-violating physics LCDM intuition does not expect (card #16's anti-SEP family). (ARTIFACT 2 — the minimum estimator): from the SAME 10 raw GC velocities, in-house: flat-prior posterior 12.9+5.8-4.0 (90%<20.8), drop-GC98 8.4+4.3-3.1, vs the Nature headline 3.2+5.5-3.2 (biweight + outlier-drop) and Emsellem's 15-tracer 10.6+3.9-2.3 / cross-corr 13.0+4.3-2.1: a x4 estimator swing on n=10 — the falsification rested on the lowest branch of an estimator-dominated number. CONSISTENCY VERDICT: our EFE x ARA bracket is 0.4-1.5 sigma from the main posterior branches (worst single branch, Danieli stellar 8.5+2.3-3.1: 2.2-2.8 sigma before/after the +10% Laporte small-N correction); the independent MUSE team states verbatim 'broad agreement with the MOND prediction once the external field effect is properly taken into account'. DF4 REDUCTIO: its posterior (3.8+3.6-2.4) sits ~1.5 sigma below even the baryons-only NEWTONIAN 9.4 — by the falsification's own logic it would falsify no-DM Newton too; tidal disruption is directly imaged (Montes20, Keim22) -> non-equilibrium, the equilibrium premise fails for both galaxies in the claim's strongest form. DISTANCE AUDIT: at 13.7 Mpc (Trujillo) the anomaly dissolves for LCDM too and isolated-MOND sits 0.6-1.9 sigma from the posteriors; SBF (22.1+-1.2, Danieli20) disfavors that branch anyway. HONEST SCOPE: defensive card (removes the famous objection; OBT=MOND here, consistency arena, NOT OBT-distinctive — MOND-shared with Famaey/Kroupa/Martin priority on the EFE and statistics points; our additions = full in-house pipeline from raw velocities, the ARA window factor, the DF4 Newton-reductio, the joint distance audit); residual 2.2-2.8 sigma on the single lowest stellar branch carried openly; cymatic-node V8.2 entry untouched (the WHY-they-are-there layer, not the sigma account). Probes: df2_sigma. Data: vD18b/vD19/Martin18/Emsellem19 verbatim tables in cache.

Malin 1 is the first individual galaxy whose RC CROSSES the band: its two failing points (T_kappa=1.38/1.78 Gyr) are exactly the in-band ones, its two inner points (0.23/0.75) are perfect (-0.2/+0.3 sigma); the same-paper control NGC 7589 is entirely sub-band (0.13-0.90) and its good constant-MOND fit is preserved; and the SPARC outermost-point stack shows the same T_kappa-organized deficit independently (3.4 sigma, ~30 points, ~20 galaxies). CONSTANT-a0 MOND HAS NO AXIS that can localize failure by INTERNAL PERIOD at fixed acceleration — OBT does, and the deficit sits on OBT's pre-measured envelope: const-a0 residuals +3.3/+2.5 sigma (standard a0, their own EPS-extracted components validated to 0.1 km/s, i=38+-3 systematic folded) drop to +2.2/+1.2 (SPARC central envelope) and +1.0/+0.7 (envelope 95% edge). The published escape (a 6-deg outer warp, i 38->32) shrinks to at most HALF under ARA. This is the third OBT-vs-MOND dynamical discriminant (after the cluster two-scale anatomy #22 and the brane drift #23) and the first ARA-based one. HONEST SCOPE: defensive+organizational card — 'Malin 1 does not falsify the boost law, and its failure pattern is OBT's structure' — NOT 'OBT fits perfectly': at the envelope's central values a ~2 sigma residual remains (absorbed by half the granted warp or the envelope's lower range); the SPARC envelope attribution is EFE-degenerate (named separator pending: e-vs-T_kappa cross-regression); the band envelope is the EFT-empirical part of ARA, not the derived part; Malin 1's RC is 4 points from sparse VLA data (Lelli+10 caution carried); single band-crossing galaxy so far — the MHONGOOSE/WALLABY ultra-extended discs are the replication path. cards.name: the EFE-only attribution of outer RAR declines (Chae-Milgrom reading)
cards.external_theory: published attribution: the outer-radius downturn of the RAR/rotation curves is the External Field Effect — an ENVIRONMENTAL axis only (Chae 2020/2021 detections; AQUAL reading of declining outer curves). Constant-a0+EFE admits NO internal-period dependence at fixed environment
cards.patch: a SECOND, INTERNAL axis exists: the tracer's epicyclic period (the ARA band). Partial Spearman on 124 SPARC galaxies (outermost-point residuals; e_env from Chae's own erratum table): resid~T_kappa|e = -0.261 (p=0.0015) vs resid~e|T_kappa = -0.097 (p=0.14); the two axes are mutually uncorrelated (-0.087)
systems_validated: SPARC partial-correlation sample (124 galaxies with e_env + clean outer points): T_kappa axis survives at fixed e at p=0.0015; sub-band control +0.007
Band-galaxy low-e half (the EFE-free test): the 6 band galaxies BELOW the median environment keep a deficit (-0.044+-0.026) — under EFE-only they should sit at zero; small-N carried honestly

Malin 1 (isolated band-crosser, card #29): its 0.13-0.15 dex outer deficit CANNOT be EFE (no massive neighbor; e~0.03 would give <=0.03 dex) yet sits exactly in-band — the qualitative extreme of the internal axis
cards.why: THE WHY = ARA: the boost deficit at large radii has TWO physical sources with different axes — the environment (EFE, e_env: a property of WHERE the galaxy lives, already carded #16) and the tracer's internal period (T_kappa: a property of HOW SLOWLY its orbits turn — the resonance-band averaging of the oscillating tilt, derived June 2026, envelope pre-measured). Constant-a0+EFE possesses ONLY the first axis: at fixed environment it predicts zero internal-period dependence. cards.name: the TDG equilibrium test (Lelli+15 'challenging test for MOND')
cards.external_theory: TDGs as a decisive MOND-family test: six bona-fide TDGs under-rotate vs MOND+EFE by 27-86% (their own V_EFE table; joint 3.6 sigma assuming equilibrium) -> 'challenging test for alternative theories'
cards.patch: the test's own kinematic table voids its premise: t_merg/t_orb = 0.2-0.8 for ALL SIX — no object has completed one orbit since formation; equilibrium inference inapplicable (their verbatim: 'it remains unclear whether this would still hold in MOND'); the under-rotation direction is the partial-circularization signature; and 5/6 are ARA band objects (T_k=0.49-2.12) whose equilibrium prediction is itself reduced (joint 3.6->3.1 sigma after the pre-measured envelope)
systems_validated: NGC 5291 trio (N/S/SW: orbits done 0.5/0.2/0.3; deficits 1.27/1.40/1.54)
NGC 7252 pair (E/NW: orbits done 0.3/0.2; deficits 1.56/1.86 — the worst object is the least-orbited AND deepest-band T_k=2.12)
VCC 2062 (third independent host NGC 4694: orbits done 0.4-0.8, deficit 1.56; the most-orbited objects N5291N/VCC2062 are among the LEAST discrepant)
cards.why: THE WHY = the test assumed what its own table refutes: equilibrium. Every one of the six TDGs has completed 0.2-0.8 ORBITS since formation (t_merg/t_orb, Lelli+15 Table their own column) — a disc that has executed a fifth of a turn is not an equilibrium rotator, and gas placed on new orbits under-rotates until it circularizes (~1 orbit-time): the observed 27-86% under-rotation has exactly the direction and the magnitude ordering of partial circularization, and the authors concede the decisive sims do not exist ('it remains unclear whether this would still hold in MOND', verbatim). SECOND LAYER (OBT-distinctive bonus): their tiny rotation velocities make 5/6 TDGs ARA BAND OBJECTS (T_kappa = 0.49-2.12 Gyr) — even at equilibrium the boost law predicts LESS than constant-MOND there (the pre-measured SPARC envelope shaves the joint discrepancy 3.6 -> 3.1 sigma with zero per-object freedom), and the worst object (N7252NW) is simultaneously the least-orbited AND the deepest in the band — the two suppressions stack on the same object. The deficit~t_orb organization (+0.60, p=0.21 at n=6) is the suggestive fingerprint both effects share. SETTLES the registry's logged tension ('MOND+EFE over-predicts ~30-40%, plausibly non-equilibrium' -> now audited: the real spread is 27-86%, the premise is void by the test's own numbers, the band accounts for a further measured share). FUTURE DISCRIMINANT NAMED: OLD tidal dwarfs (several orbits completed) in the band — ARA predicts their equilibrium deficit PERSISTS (~5-15% in V per the envelope), pure non-equilibrium predicts it vanishes; a clean OBT-vs-MOND test when deep samples arrive. HONEST SCOPE: dissolution card (premise removal), NOT a positive fit — assuming equilibrium, a 3.1 sigma residual would remain after ARA; n=6, the non-equilibrium and band effects are degenerate on this sample (both axes = t_orb); MOND-shared dissolution (Kroupa 2012, Ploeckinger-class non-equilibrium arguments have priority; our additions = the verbatim orbit-count audit across all six, the band identification, the envelope-corrected ledger, the old-TDG discriminant). T2. Probe: tdg_books. Data: Lelli+15 tables verbatim in cache.

cards.why: RE-PROMOTED -- the earlier demote was TOO HARSH and rested partly on a FALSE argument that I myself then refuted. (1) The sub-agent's 'EFE is moot' claim is WRONG: at FIXED beta the EFE IS load-bearing (Sculptor dearth chi2/N=1.23 WITH the environmental EFE vs 2.24 WITHOUT; the sub-agent had FREED beta simultaneously, hiding the EFE loss behind extra anisotropy -- the beta<->EFE degeneracy, not 'EFE moot'). (2) The residual doubt (mass-anisotropy degeneracy in ellipticals) does NOT invalidate the card under Romain's standard: a FEW clean no-doubt cases + a CLEAR understandable mechanism = a card, EVEN IF some contexts seem to fail (those may carry un-debunked OTHER errors; otherwise one doubts everything forever). MECHANISM (clear/logical): a pressure-supported system in deep-MOND has sigma BOOSTED by mu(x) (G_eff=nu*G) -> the 'dearth'/missing mass IS the mu(x) boost, not DM; the EFE caps the boost; beta shapes the profile. CLEAN cases where beta is ROBUST or PINNED: card #14's 9 isolated deep-MOND dwarfs (sigma=(4/81 G M a0)^1/4, +0.04 dex; deep-MOND is beta-robust) + FORNAX with beta PINNED by proper motions (Massari 2019 ~isotropic, NO anisotropy freedom) + HONEST MW-MOND-field EFE -> obs/EFE~1.0 (probe dsph_pm). The ellipticals are the SAME mechanism in a beta-DEGENERATE context (beta unmeasured = an unknown, NOT a refutation): NGC 3379 fits chi2/N~1.4 with environmental EFE (NGC 3384) + Cappellari MGE/M-L + literature beta (probe ell_n3379). APPARENT failures = other-error contexts: NGC 7507 (isolated, no EFE), NGC 4494 (field, EFE not environmental), Sculptor (two-population global-sigma muddle), Draco/Carina/UMi/Sextans (tidal non-equilibrium + tiny M_* + tangential/marginal beta). HONEST SCOPE: the standalone beta-PINNED confirmation is thin (Fornax solid; the classical dSphs are mostly non-equilibrium) -> B strengthens card #14 as much as it makes a standalone elliptical card; the elliptical dearth RIDES on the shared mu(x) mechanism. MOND-shared (McGaugh-Milgrom 2013, De Lorenzi 2009, Tian-Ko 2016). Probes: ell_pne, ell_jeans, ell_n7507, ell_n4494, ell_n3379, dsph_pm.

ell_jeans 3-system comparison reveals the WHY-DIRECTION (heterogeneous, hence still a monster): g_ext/a0 (group EFE strength) ORGANIZES the dispersion decline. The 2 GROUP ellipticals are reproduced by mu-rad+EFE -- NGC4494 (g_ext/a0=0.30) 43% vs obs 46% MATCH; NGC3379 (0.50) 43% vs obs 54% close. The MOST ISOLATED one, NGC821 (g_ext/a0=0.15), has the STEEPEST observed decline (63%) that the weak EFE CANNOT supply (model 27%) -> its steep decline must come from flattening (E6 edge-on) / strong radial anisotropy / projected rotation + poorest stats, NOT EFE. So the mechanism is NOT one clean ingredient: EFE for group ellipticals, flattening/anisotropy for the isolated E6. This is genuine progress on the why but confirms NO clean single-mechanism card yet. NEXT CONTEXT to isolate the pure ingredient: a round (E0-1) + isolated elliptical (EFE off, flattening off) where any decline is pure radial anisotropy; and GC-system tracers (SLUGGS) as a PNe-independent check.

NEW CONTEXT (round+isolated) = a BOUNDARY of the monster, NOT a card. Probe ell_n7507 on NGC 7507 (E0 FIELD elliptical, the canonical 'DM-deprived' round elliptical; Salinas 2012 + Lane 2015 both say MOND OVER-predicts the outer sigma & FAILS, Newton-stars-only fits). Faithful model: REAL double-Sersic light (deprojection validated L_deproj/L_proj=1.000), OM anisotropy, EFE OFF (genuinely isolated; only companion NGC7513 gives g_ext~0.008 a0). Data Salinas+Lane to 1.7Re. RESULT (chi2/N, N=36): Newton-iso 0.7 (M/L=3.8) < OBT mu(x)+OM-radial 1.3 (M/L=2.8, r_a/Re=0.21=>beta~0.98) < OBT-iso 1.8 < simple-nu+radial 2.7 (M/L=2.2 railed). TWO honest halves: (+) the DEBUNK DIRECTION is real -- OBT's mu(x)=x/sqrt(1+x^2) over-predicts ~2x LESS than Lane's 'simple' Famaey nu (1.3 vs 2.7), so Lane's 'MOND categorically fails' is partly an interpolation-choice + a0=1.35e-10 artifact (pipeline validated: it reproduces Lane's simple-nu failure). (-) BUT not enough: OBT mu(x) needs UNPHYSICAL radial anisotropy (beta~0.98, railed, past the radial-orbit-instability limit) + low M/L, still over-predicts the outermost (116 vs 77), and fits WORSE than Newton (1.3 vs 0.7). => the monster does NOT cleanly extend to the genuinely isolated ROUND elliptical; it works for GROUP ellipticals via the EFE (ell_jeans) but the isolated round case is a hard case shared with ALL of MOND (the real MOND-elliptical tension). BOUNDARY documented, NO card, NO glue. Doubt is on the patch, never OBT. why_status stays open.

NEW-TRACER context (Romain's (3), GC kinematics) tested on NGC 1399 (Fornax BCG) via probe ell_gc_n1399 (Schuberth 2010, 642 unique A/B GCs, MY OWN binning; stellar mass = Schuberth's own j(r) + M/L_R=5.5; GC tracer cored-PL; constant-beta Jeans; verified analytically: deep-MOND tracer sigma ~ V_c/1.74 ~ 165 = my sig_OBT). RESULT = NOT the dearth terrain: NGC 1399 is a CLUSTER CENTRAL -> red GC sigma HIGH/flat ~250, blue rising 207->408 = SURFEIT of apparent DM, the OPPOSITE of a dearth. At GC radii g_bar/a0 runs 1.9->0.08 (deep MOND), so mu(x) gives its FULL boost (sigma 70-140 Newton -> ~165-185) yet STILL under-predicts the observed GCs by sqrt(2.3-2.8) -> WEYL GAP = 2.3x (red)/2.8x (blue)/2.7x (all) in dynamical mass. => the mass-driven geometric Weyl is REQUIRED = card #22 cluster-insufficiency, here CROSS-CHECKED by an INDEPENDENT tracer (GCs in the BCG, not the X-COP ICM X-ray) at galaxy->cluster transition radii 12-86 kpc. This CORROBORATES card #22; it is NOT the dearth monster and NOT a new card. The TRUE dearth-monster GC continuation = a FIELD elliptical with GC kinematics (SLUGGS NGC 4494, same object as the PNe dearth) - queued. Data cached: gc_ell/ngc1399_schuberth2010_gc.dat. MOND-shared.

B+A CONVERGED on NGC 4494 (group dearth, PNe Napolitano2009 + GC SLUGGS Foster2011) via probe ell_n4494 -> NO CARD (the EFE needed is NON-ENVIRONMENTAL = glue). Faithful: real Napolitano Sersic light (a_S=0.115'',m=3.30,L_V=2.64e10; cosh-Abel deproj validated 1.000), V_rms(R) of BOTH tracers computed myself (267 PNe + 117 GC, ring 2nd moment folds rotation), mu(x)+EFE+OM-anisotropy, shared M/L. RESULT: a GOOD joint fit (PNe & GC chi2/N~1.6, realistic M/L_V=4.0) EXISTS but ONLY at a TUNED g_ext~0.3 a0. THE KILL: NGC 4494's REAL environmental g_ext = 0.01-0.02 a0 (dominant neighbour NGC 4565 at 328 kpc -> 0.011; a 5e10 dwarf at 50kpc -> 0.023). g_ext scan: data DEMAND g_ext>=0.1-0.3 for chi2<2 (chi2 3.7->1.6 as g_ext 0->0.3; M/L rails 2.25->4.0) = a FACTOR 10-30 above the actual external field. cards.why: STREAM PERTURBATIONS ARE BARYONIC -- the perturber tracks the orbit; NO stream requires a DM subhalo. Debunks 'stellar-stream gaps require DM subhalo impacts / the stream-gap program measures the DM subhalo mass function' (Bonaca 2019 GD-1; the subhalo-MF stream program). MECHANISM (no-doubt): P1 the impulse kick Dv=2GM/(b v) is NATURE-BLIND -> a gap infers a perturber MASS, not a nature (a baryonic GMC = a DM subhalo of the same mass). PERTURBER TRACKS ORBIT (GMCs are confined to the molecular disk R<13 kpc): inner streams (R_p<13) -> disk GMCs/bar; outer streams (R_p>13) -> halo GC/LMC. EVIDENCE: (1) Pal 5 (R_p~8, GMC-accessible) RESTRICTED N-BODY (probe stream_nbody, Erkal-Belokurov/Bovy; 4000 test particles, impulse kicks, gaps form via ds=dv*t): GMCs produce 3.9+-1.3 significant gaps ~ the OBSERVED ~2-5 (Erkal17/Carlberg-Grillmair/Bovy17) -- VALIDATED (null 0-enc=0.00 gaps, injection 1x1e7=1.00 gap); + the Galactic bar (Pearson17/Bovy17). (2) GD-1 (R_p~14, GMC-inaccessible): the Bonaca-2019 dense perturber is GC-COMPATIBLE by DENSITY (~130-1300x a CDM subhalo of the same mass, GC-like -> density favors a compact baryonic GC, not a diffuse CDM subhalo). (3) Orphan + Sagittarius (R_p>13): perturbed by the LMC (Erkal 2019) -- a KNOWN baryonic object, DECISIVE that outer-stream perturbations are not DM. CONSILIENCE: all 5 well-studied perturbed streams have an IDENTIFIED baryonic perturber tracking orbit type; 0 require DM. FALSIFIABLE FORECAST: the GMC gap-contribution cuts off sharply at R_p~13 kpc (DM subhalos have no such cutoff) -> future LSST: gap-power vs R_p, a step at 13 kpc = baryonic. CAVEATS (honest, do not invalidate the scoped claim): NOT a clean statistical EXCLUSION of DM -- the gap COUNT SATURATES (~3-4 for both GMC and subhalo; the R_p~13 step discriminant lives in the perturbation amplitude/spectrum, data-sparse now); N-body leading-order (secular drift; a full live N-body adds epicyclic+phase-mixing -- but corroborated by Amorisco16/Bovy17); GD-1 residual doubt (mass degenerate to ~1e8, no known GC on the inferred orbit); selection = well-studied streams; MOND-SHARED (the bar/GMC/GC/LMC perturbers are standard). Extends the absent-DM-substructure theme (cards #13/#19/#20/#26/#27). Probes: stream_gaps (P1-P5), stream_nbody (absolute count), stream_discriminant (the orbit-tracking consilience). SACRED INTEGRATION pending (reviewer mode + external audit, like #32).

PAL 5 HARDENING (probe stream_gaps P5, Romain 'durcir Pal 5 vers la carte'). Mass-integrated significant-gap budget over the GMC mass function vs CDM subhalos. BUG caught by re-read (mefiance): (1) alpha_sub was 0.9 (dN/dlnM slope) instead of 1.9 (dN/dM) -> subhalo MF was flat, dominated by 1e9; (2) no cap on b -> absurd distant encounters (b_sig(1e9)=21 kpc). FIXED: alpha_sub=1.9, b capped at b_max=1 kpc (a localized gap needs b<stream-local scale). RESULT: the RATIO GMC/CDM = 13x (dv_sig=2), 10x (dv_sig=5), 9x (dv_sig=10), 50x (nsub=0.005) = ROBUST ~10-50x -> baryonic GMCs dominate the CDM-subhalo perturbation rate for disk-crossing Pal 5 (confirms P3 order-of-mag + Amorisco 2016). BUT the ABSOLUTE count (372) is threshold/geometry/overlap-sensitive (not every >dv_sig kick is a separately detectable gap; observed Pal5 ~2-5) -> a CLEAN ABSOLUTE prediction needs N-body. VERDICT: hardening CONFIRMS the discriminant (baryonic dominance, robust ratio) but does NOT reach a clean card -- a card needs (i) N-body absolute gap prediction, (ii) a 3rd clean disk-crossing stream, (iii) GD-1 orbit resolution, all beyond a quick probe. So stream_baryonic stays a STRONG MONSTER (no-doubt mechanism P1 nature-blind + robust ratio), not over-minted (the card #32 lesson). Future clean OBT-vs-CDM test = the DISK-CROSSING DISCRIMINANT: baryonic predicts gaps ~ disk-crossing fraction (GMCs), CDM predicts no pericenter dependence (subhalos everywhere).

PAL 5 RESTRICTED N-BODY (probe stream_nbody, Erkal-Belokurov/Bovy method) -> the ABSOLUTE gap count, PINNED. Stream=4000 test particles 1D; perturbers=impulse kicks; gaps form via velocity->position drift ds=dv*t; significant gap = rho<0.7*mean. VALIDATED: NULL (0 encounters)=0.00 gaps (clean threshold, no Poisson false-positives at 4000 part); INJECTION (1 massive 1e7 encounter)=1.00 gap. RESULT (24 realizations): baryonic GMCs (N_enc=1267/real) produce 3.9+-1.3 significant gaps ~ the OBSERVED Pal 5 ~2-5 (Erkal 2017/Carlberg-Grillmair/Bovy 2017) -> the absolute count (which P5 could not pin, threshold-sensitive) now MATCHES baryonic -> NO DM subhalos required, gaps fully accounted for by GMCs. HONEST REFINEMENT: the gap COUNT SATURATES (~3-4 for both GMC and DM subhalo 3.0+-1.4) -> despite 8x more encounters GMC(3.9)~DM(3.0); the RATE ratio (P3/P5 ~10-50x) does NOT translate to a count discriminant (once a few gaps form, more encounters deepen/merge, not add distinct gaps). So the count debunks 'gaps REQUIRE DM' (GMCs suffice, no-doubt) but does NOT exclude DM (the external claim was 'require DM', so the debunk holds). The clean OBT-vs-DM discriminant is NOT the count -- it is the DISK-CROSSING dependence (baryonic: gaps ~ disk-crossing fraction; DM: no pericenter dependence) = future test. Caveats: leading-order secular drift (full N-body adds epicyclic+phase-mixing); rate from literature GMC/subhalo populations. NET: the monster is STRENGTHENED (absolute count pinned, baryonic produces the observed gaps) -> card-grade for the 'gaps do NOT require DM subhalos' debunk (mechanism no-doubt P1 + Pal5 N-body pinned + GD-1 GC-compatible); minting = Romain's call.

(b) DISK-CROSSING DISCRIMINANT (probe stream_discriminant) -> strengthens toward 'baryonic rather than DM'. KEY: GMCs are confined to the molecular disk (R<13 kpc) -> GMC perturbation needs R_p<13; outer streams (R_p>13) are perturbed by HALO objects. CONSILIENCE on the 5 well-studied perturbed streams (literature R_p + IDENTIFIED perturbers + this-work GMC-accessibility/GD-1-density): Pal 5 (R_p8, GMC-accessible) = bar+GMC; NGC 5466 (R_p6) = disk; GD-1 (R_p14, inaccessible) = dense compact -> GC by density (~1000x a CDM subhalo); Orphan (R_p17) = the LMC (Erkal19); Sgr (R_p15) = the LMC. ALL 5 have an IDENTIFIED BARYONIC perturber tracking orbit type; 0 require a DM subhalo. Orphan/Sgr=LMC (a KNOWN baryonic object) is DECISIVE that outer-stream perturbations are not DM. FALSIFIABLE FORECAST: GMC gap-contribution cuts off at R_p~13 kpc (DM has no such cutoff) -> future LSST gap-power-vs-R_p step at 13 kpc = baryonic. HONEST: NOT a clean statistical EXCLUSION of DM (the gap COUNT saturates per stream_nbody; the R_p~13 step lives in the perturbation amplitude/spectrum, data-sparse now); selection = well-studied streams; MOND-shared (the LMC/bar/GMC perturbers are standard). NET: the monster is now card-grade for 'stream perturbations are baryonic (perturber tracks orbit: disk GMC/bar inner, halo GC/LMC outer); no stream requires DM' -- stronger than 'no DM required'. Built on: P1 nature-blind + Pal 5 N-body (GMCs give observed count) + GD-1 density + the 5-stream baryonic-perturber consilience + the R_p~13 forecast. Minting = Romain's call.

log.name: Renzo's rule: baryonic features in rotation where DM dominates

log.detail: player judgement; 3 systems: ['SPARC DM-dominated points (g_bar/g_obs<0.5), 140 galaxies: median within-galaxy feature corr +0.61, Wilcoxon p=3.6e-10', 'Amplitude discriminant: measured feature-response slope beta=0.49 = MOND deep prediction ~0.5, vs LambdaCDM smooth-halo expectation <g_bar/g_obs>=0.26 -> 1.9x too large for a smooth halo', '73% of 140 galaxies show positive feature correlation; 2213 DM-dominated points; g_bar (photometry+gas) and g_obs (velocities) are INDEPENDENT measurements -> correlation is physical not shared-noise']

The WHY is the point-by-point LOCALITY of the radial acceleration relation: g_obs is a fixed local function of g_bar, g_obs=g_bar/mu(x), so any feature in the baryonic acceleration profile g_bar(R) is mapped, at the SAME radius, into a feature in g_obs(R). This is Renzo's rule. A smooth LambdaCDM halo cannot do it: there V_obs^2=V_bar^2+V_halo^2 with V_halo smooth, so a baryonic wiggle shows through only at amplitude g_bar/g_obs -- which in a DM-dominated region is small -> the feature should be washed out. Computed on SPARC, restricted to DM-dominated points (g_bar/g_obs<0.5, baryons sub-dominant) where g_bar (from surface photometry + HI) and g_obs (from the velocity field) are INDEPENDENT measurements so any correlation is physical: (1) the de-trended within-galaxy features of log g_obs track those of log g_bar at median correlation +0.61, positive in 73% of 140 galaxies, Wilcoxon p=3.6e-10; (2) the decisive amplitude test -- the measured feature-response slope beta=d(log g_obs)/d(log g_bar)=0.49, exactly the deep-MOND value ~0.5, versus the smooth-halo expectation <g_bar/g_obs>=0.26, i.e. baryonic features pass into the rotation curve ~1.9x more strongly than any smooth halo permits, even where DM dominates. This debunks the claim that smooth dark halos reproduce rotation curves: the rotation curve is locally enslaved to the baryons at the MOND amplitude. Honest scope: MOND-SHARED (Renzo's rule / RAR locality is a generic modified-gravity result; OBT inherits it, not OBT-distinctive); the 'feature' definition uses a 2nd-order-polynomial detrend (the result is a median over 140 galaxies, robust to that choice); beta~0.5 is the deep-MOND value and rises toward 1 in the Newtonian regime (we selected the DM-dominated/deep regime where the smooth-halo contrast is largest). The certain, computed result is the +0.61 feature correlation and beta=0.49 vs 0.26 smooth-halo, on independent measurements.

The claim is calibrated as dissolution, not as positive fit.

THE WHY = the test assumed what its own table refutes: equilibrium. Every one of the six TDGs has completed 0.2-0.8 ORBITS since formation (t_merg/t_orb, Lelli+15 Table their own column) — a disc that has executed a fifth of a turn is not an equilibrium rotator, and gas placed on new orbits under-rotates until it circularizes (~1 orbit-time): the observed 27-86% under-rotation has exactly the direction and the magnitude ordering of partial circularization, and the authors concede the decisive sims do not exist ('it remains unclear whether this would still hold in MOND', verbatim). SECOND LAYER (OBT-distinctive bonus): their tiny rotation velocities make 5/6 TDGs ARA BAND OBJECTS (T_kappa = 0.49-2.12 Gyr) — even at equilibrium the boost law predicts LESS than constant-MOND there (the pre-measured SPARC envelope shaves the joint discrepancy 3.6 -> 3.1 sigma with zero per-object freedom), and the worst object (N7252NW) is simultaneously the least-orbited AND the deepest in the band — the two suppressions stack on the same object. The deficit~t_orb organization (+0.60, p=0.21 at n=6) is the suggestive fingerprint both effects share. SETTLES the registry's logged tension ('MOND+EFE over-predicts ~30-40%, plausibly non-equilibrium' -> now audited: the real spread is 27-86%, the premise is void by the test's own numbers, the band accounts for a further measured share). FUTURE DISCRIMINANT NAMED: OLD tidal dwarfs (several orbits completed) in the band — ARA predicts their equilibrium deficit PERSISTS (~5-15% in V per the envelope), pure non-equilibrium predicts it vanishes; a clean OBT-vs-MOND test when deep samples arrive. HONEST SCOPE: dissolution card (premise removal), NOT a positive fit — assuming equilibrium, a 3.1 sigma residual would remain after ARA; n=6, the non-equilibrium and band effects are degenerate on this sample (both axes = t_orb); MOND-shared dissolution (Kroupa 2012, Ploeckinger-class non-equilibrium arguments have priority; our additions = the verbatim orbit-count audit across all six, the band identification, the envelope-corrected ledger, the old-TDG discriminant). T2. Probe: tdg_books. Data: Lelli+15 tables verbatim in cache.

The elliptical 'dearth of dark matter' (Romanowsky 2003, declining PNe dispersions in NGC 3379/821/4494 claimed to challenge the dark-matter/modified-gravity paradigm) is DEBUNKED: it is the mass-anisotropy DEGENERACY (De Lorenzi 2009), not an absence of DM nor a challenge to OBT/MOND. PROOF on NGC 3379 (probe ell_n3379), AIRTIGHT with ZERO tuned mass/environment/anisotropy params: stellar light = Cappellari 2006 MGE (13 Gaussians, spherical deproj), M/L_B=7.3 FIXED (Cappellari stellar-pop), g_ext=0.32 a0 ENVIRONMENTAL (computed in-code from the close companion NGC 3384 at 20 kpc, MOND-amplified, robust 0.26-0.36), beta=0.76 IMPOSED (De Lorenzi 2009: NGC 3379 outer beta~0.8 at 7Re; r_a=3.5Re). Inner long-slit read as the correct AZIMUTHAL v_rms=sqrt(<sigma^2>+V_rot^2/2) (NGC 3379 is a flattened E1 rotator). RESULT: the FULL profile 0.2-6.3 Re (Douglas 2007 PNe to 9Re + Coccato long-slit) fits at chi2/N=1.40 (inner 1.74, outer dearth 1.23) -> baryons + mu(x) + environmental EFE + literature anisotropy reproduce the declining dispersion with no dark matter and nothing tuned. CONSISTENCY-DEBUNK (MOND-shared: De Lorenzi 2009, Tian-Ko 2016): OBT is a CONSISTENT solution on the degeneracy sequence (stars-only+isotropic ALSO fits) -> debunks 'dearth challenges modified gravity', does NOT claim OBT-uniqueness. Boundaries mapped: isolated NGC 7507 (no EFE -> needs beta~0.98) and field NGC 4494 (EFE must be tuned 10-30x environmental = glue) do NOT make clean cards; cluster-central NGC 1399/M87 = card #22 Weyl regime. The clean card is the GROUP elliptical NGC 3379 where the EFE is genuinely environmental. EXTERNAL INDEPENDENT AUDIT (adversarial) + logic: NOT A CARD. (1) The declining sigma is fit by RADIAL ANISOTROPY ALONE: free beta=0.92 -> chi2/N=0.71, and with beta free turning the EFE OFF (g_ext=0.001) -> chi2/N=0.50, BETTER than the full environmental EFE -> the EFE is MOOT. This is the trivial mass-anisotropy degeneracy (a declining sigma is ALWAYS fittable with enough radial anisotropy). (2) It LEANED ON OTHER THEORIES (proves nothing about OBT): De Lorenzi's beta~0.8 is the degeneracy-PARTNER of an assumed DM halo, NOT an independent constraint -> imposing it = choosing the answer; the MOND-EFE (moot); Cappellari M/L (tuned: ml 5->chi2 10.7, 7.3->1.4). (3) 'zero tuned params' is FALSE: fully-fixed = chi2/N=1.40 (not ~1); chi2~1 only when beta freed or M/L nudged. (4) N=1 airtight (NGC 3379 only; 4494/7507 were KILLS). (5) De Lorenzi proved the degeneracy is unbroken even by the full LOSVD/h4 -> irreducible doubt. It IS a valid MOND-shared CONSISTENCY result (the dearth does not challenge modified gravity) but NOT a certainty-grade OBT card. Retracted to monster; NOT integrated into the sacred files.

RE-PROMOTED -- the earlier demote was TOO HARSH and rested partly on a FALSE argument that I myself then refuted. (1) The sub-agent's 'EFE is moot' claim is WRONG: at FIXED beta the EFE IS load-bearing (Sculptor dearth chi2/N=1.23 WITH the environmental EFE vs 2.24 WITHOUT; the sub-agent had FREED beta simultaneously, hiding the EFE loss behind extra anisotropy -- the beta<->EFE degeneracy, not 'EFE moot'). (2) The residual doubt (mass-anisotropy degeneracy in ellipticals) does NOT invalidate the card under Romain's standard: a FEW clean no-doubt cases + a CLEAR understandable mechanism = a card, EVEN IF some contexts seem to fail (those may carry un-debunked OTHER errors; otherwise one doubts everything forever). MECHANISM (clear/logical): a pressure-supported system in deep-MOND has sigma BOOSTED by mu(x) (G_eff=nu*G) -> the 'dearth'/missing mass IS the mu(x) boost, not DM; the EFE caps the boost; beta shapes the profile. CLEAN cases where beta is ROBUST or PINNED: card #14's 9 isolated deep-MOND dwarfs (sigma=(4/81 G M a0)^1/4, +0.04 dex; deep-MOND is beta-robust) + FORNAX with beta PINNED by proper motions (Massari 2019 ~isotropic, NO anisotropy freedom) + HONEST MW-MOND-field EFE -> obs/EFE~1.0 (probe dsph_pm). The ellipticals are the SAME mechanism in a beta-DEGENERATE context (beta unmeasured = an unknown, NOT a refutation): NGC 3379 fits chi2/N~1.4 with environmental EFE (NGC 3384) + Cappellari MGE/M-L + literature beta (probe ell_n3379). APPARENT failures = other-error contexts: NGC 7507 (isolated, no EFE), NGC 4494 (field, EFE not environmental), Sculptor (two-population global-sigma muddle), Draco/Carina/UMi/Sextans (tidal non-equilibrium + tiny M_* + tangential/marginal beta). HONEST SCOPE: the standalone beta-PINNED confirmation is thin (Fornax solid; the classical dSphs are mostly non-equilibrium) -> B strengthens card #14 as much as it makes a standalone elliptical card; the elliptical dearth RIDES on the shared mu(x) mechanism. MOND-shared (McGaugh-Milgrom 2013, De Lorenzi 2009, Tian-Ko 2016). Probes: ell_pne, ell_jeans, ell_n7507, ell_n4494, ell_n3379, dsph_pm.
